newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The public works department's programme to develop a register of state-owned properties has shown that government owns 130,000 properties with a maintenance backlog of R8,8 billion and a collection of secret properties it never knew it owned.

- Oil companies operating in South Africa should be prepared to relinquish their "tie agreements" -- which prevent petrol station owners from switching readily from one brand to another -- if the oil market is freed in terms of proposed industry regulations, says Minerals and Energy Minister Penuell Maduna.

- If a group of Sandton businesses succeeded in immediately overturning substantial increases in their municipal rates, there would be "major disruption" to services in Johannesburg, the city's metropolitan council warned in court papers.

- Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau paved the way for possible foreign control of privatised Sun Air yesterday, increasing the stake available to offshore buyers to 49 percent from the original 25 percent.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Federal-Mogul SA, the 750 million rand South African subsidiary of the US-based vehicle spares group, is up for sale, says managing director Claude Mencotti.

- South Africa's gold production dropped by 27 tonnes to a 40-year low of 495 tonnes last year, costing the country 1,5 billion rand in lost revenue and foreign exchange earnings, the Chamber of Mines said.
- The rand reached its best level against the dollar since late July yesterday, briefly dipping below the 4,40 rand bid in after-hours trade.

- Omega Holdings Ltd is set to acquire Tek, the low margin consumer electronic arm of Plessey Corp Ltd, for about 70 million rand, market sources said yesterday. The companies have issued cautionary notices to shareholders.

- Foreign investors will be able to buy 49 percent of Sun Air, the state-owned airline, rather than the 25 percent previously offered for sale, Stella Sigcau, the minister for public enterprises, said yesterday.
SAKE BEELD
- The rand reached best levels yesterday to 4.40 rand against the U.S. dollar. It is against its highest since July 23 last year.
- Ferro-alloy producer Samancor announces that its attributable income for the six months to end-December plunged to 171.43 million rand from 381.92 million rand attained in the same period in 1995.
THE STAR
- More than 100 prisoners are escaping each month as understaffed and ill-equipped Department of Correctional Services personnel battle to plug growing loopholes in the justice system.
- Willem Ratte, the ex-soldier who "captured" Fort Schanskop near Pretoria in 1993, was arrested with 11 others yesterday while allegedly trying to steal weapons and ammunition from an army base.

- Pay station M-Net has hit out at allegations that one of its senior employees, a former general manager at the SABC, was involved in irregularities which helped its sport channel, Supersport, win a 5,4 million rand contract from the Confederation of African Football (CAF) to screen next year's African Cup of Nations soccer tournament.
